sources.locator: Complete 31-page paper retrieved. Read §3, equations (44)–(47), printed pp. 8–9 (PDF pp. 9–10), for the symplectic current, integrated pre-symplectic form, and boundary ambiguity.

contents.name: Equations (44)–(47): symplectic current and integrated pre-symplectic form
contents.support: The local fixed-background definition adopts the antisymmetrized current and explicitly separates its chosen normalization from action prefactors.

contents.name: Convergence and asymptotic falloff at spatial infinity
contents.reason: The assigned items state convergence only when needed and impose no asymptotic-flatness or infinite-region falloff theorem.

sources.locator: Complete 61-page paper retrieved. Read §3.3, “Maxwell theory,” equations (3.18)–(3.25), printed pp. 26–27 (PDF pp. 27–28), including the variation, current, gauge direction, and boundary charge.

contents.name: §3.3, equations (3.18)–(3.22): Maxwell variation and pre-symplectic form
contents.support: The definition states the fixed-metric Maxwell current on global normalized connection variations and leaves the action normalization explicit.

contents.name: §3.3, equations (3.23)–(3.25): gauge flow and boundary electric charge
contents.support: The local proof derives the exact current change, integrates it over a finite smooth chain, and keeps the boundary flux rather than declaring every gauge direction degenerate.

contents.name: §1.3.1: field-space current and its integration
contents.support: The connection-normalized formula is written with its own explicit sign and normalization, with no full phase-space manifold claim.

contents.name: §§1.3.2–1.3.3: gravitational diffeomorphism charges and surface-charge identity
contents.reason: The assigned boundary lemma treats the abelian Maxwell block and proves its boundary term; it does not construct gravitational diffeomorphism charges or Hamiltonian generators.

contents.name: §2.4, Proposition 2.20: quotient by the kernel of a restricted symplectic form

contents.name: §2.4, Proposition 2.22: reduction of Lagrangian subspaces
